newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open little changed Tuesday on the heels of an uninspiring performance in London, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures were slightly higher early Tuesday in thin rangebound dealings. LIFFE July cocoa was up four stg at the midday break at 1,023 stg a tonne, traded 1,023 to 1,019 stg. Sepember was up three stg at 1,040 stg.

Monday, New York cocoa futures finished broadly higher in slim dealings, bolstered by a late-session round of local shortcovering. July ended up $10 at $1,477 a tonne after trading between $1,480 and $1,458. Second-month September closed $11 lower at $1,504, while the remaining months slumped $12 to $15.
Technically, traders said July would face some initial support near $1,460 to $1,458, with the next level pegged at $1,445 to $1,441. Resistance was seen at the $1,494 to $1,501 gap on the charts.

On the fundamental side, German cocoa bean imports from third countries in January 1997 totaled 15,263 tonnes after 17,965 tonnes in December 1996 and 17,009 in January 1996, federal statistics office data showed on Tuesday. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
